newsitem.title: USA: New England Elec in $1.59 bln deal with PG&E.
newsitem.headline: New England Elec in $1.59 bln deal with PG&E.

text.p: New England Electric System said on Wednesday it agreed to sell its non-nuclear generating business to an affiliate of PG&E Corp for $1.59 billion in cash.
The deal would result in an average price drop of about 15 percent for New England Electric's 1.3 million customers, the utility said.
In anticipation of the proceeds from the deal, New England Electric said in a news release that it authorized the repurchase of up to 5 million of its common shares.

The agreement calls for New England Electric's New England Power Co and Narragansett Electric Co subsidiaries to sell 18 power plants and 23 power contract obligations to PG&E affiliate U.S. Generating Co. The deal would reduce New England Electric's "stranded investment," paying off nearly all of its fossil, hydro and nuclear power plant investments, the company said.
The $1.59 billion includes $225 million to be paid when customer choice of power supplier is widely available in New England. That amount begins to decline if choice is not available by Jan. 1, 1999.

New England Power would pay between $150 million and $170 million annually through January 2008 to offset the above-market portion of power purchase contracts assumed by U.S. Generating. And New England Electric and its units would receive an additional $85 million to cover costs from early retirement, special severance and re-training programs for employees affected by industry restructuring.
The deal must be approved by state and federal regulators, with decisions expected in 1998, the company said.
